tweets: Missing access controls let malicious parties withdraw Ether from a contract account.
This risk often stems from unintentionally exposing initialization functions.
Wrongly naming a function as a constructor places its code in runtime bytecode.
Anyone can then call that exposed constructor to re-initialize the contract.
Reviewers should verify all state-changing functions have proper access modifiers.
Ensure no unintended entry points exist in your contract's initialization logic.
